passages.text: For the Years Ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition, results of operations and related information for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , including applicable year-to-year comparisons, should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes included under Part II, Item 8 of this annual report. Our financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) in the United States (“U.S.”). Discussion and analysis of matters pertaining to the year ended December 31, 2023 and year-to-year comparisons between the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 are not included in this Form 10-K, but can be found under Part II, Item 7 of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 that was filed on February 28, 2025 . Key References Used in this Management’s Discussion and Analysis Unless the context requires otherwise, references to “we,” “us” or “our” within this annual report are intended to mean the business and operations of Enterprise Products Partners L.P. and its consolidated subsidiaries. References to the “Partnership” or “Enterprise” mean Enterprise Products Partners L.P. on a standalone basis. References to “EPO” mean Enterprise Products Operating LLC, which is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Partnership, and its consolidated subsidiaries, through which the Partnership conducts its business. We are managed by our general partner, Enterprise Products Holdings LLC (“Enterprise GP”), which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Dan Duncan LLC, a privately held Texas limited liability company. The membership interests of Dan Duncan LLC are owned by a voting trust, the current trustees (“DD LLC Trustees”) of which are: (i) Randa Duncan Williams, who is also a director and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Enterprise GP (the “Board”); (ii) Richard H. Bachmann, who is also a director and Vice Chairman of the Board; and (iii) W. Randall Fowler, who is also a director and a Co-Chief Executive Officer of Enterprise GP. Ms. Duncan Williams and Messrs. Bachmann and Fowler also currently serve as managers of Dan Duncan LLC. References to “EPCO” mean Enterprise Products Company, a privately held Texas corporation, and its privately held affiliates. The outstanding voting capital stock of EPCO is owned by a voting trust, the current trustees (“EPCO Trustees”) of which are: (i) Ms. Duncan Williams, who serves as Chairman of EPCO; (ii) Mr. Bachmann, who serves as the President and Chief Executive Officer of EPCO; and (iii) Mr. Fowler, who serves as an Executive Vice President and the Chief Financial Officer of EPCO. Ms. Duncan Williams and Messrs. Bachmann and Fowler also currently serve as directors of EPCO. We, Enterprise GP, EPCO and Dan Duncan LLC are affiliates under the collective common control of the DD LLC Trustees and the EPCO Trustees. EPCO, together with its privately held affiliates, owned approximately 32.5% of the Partnership’s common units outstanding at December 31, 2025 . Current Outlook As noted previously, this annual report on Form 10-K, including this update to our outlook on business conditions, contains forward-looking statements that are based on our beliefs and those of Enterprise GP. In addition, it reflects assumptions made by us and information currently available to us, which includes forecast information published by third parties. See “Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Information” within this Part II, Item 7 and “Risk Factors” in Part I, Item 1A, for additional information. The following information in this Current Outlook presents our current views on key midstream energy supply and demand fundamentals, and is qualified in all respects as forward-looking statements whether or not expressly qualified as such in particular sentences. All references to U.S. Energy Information Administration (“EIA”) forecasts and expectations are derived from its February 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook (“February 2026 STEO”), which was published on February 10, 2026. The level of services we provide and the amount of hydrocarbons we purchase and sell continue to be driven by supply and demand fundamentals for hydrocarbon products. These dynamics affect our financial position, results of operations and cash flows. Entering 2026, global liquid hydrocarbon markets have shifted into a modest surplus as non-Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (“non-OPEC”) supply growth, together with the scheduled easing of OPEC and Russia (collectively, the “OPEC+” group) production cuts, have contributed to inventory builds and placed downward pressure on liquid hydrocarbon prices relative to levels seen during 2024 and 2025. Against this backdrop, broader macroeconomic conditions remain a key determinant of hydrocarbon demand. Global economic growth, an important driver of demand, remains resilient but moderate. In its January 2026 World Economic Outlook, the International Monetary Fund (“IMF”) projects global economic growth of 3.3% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 as headline inflation continues to ease. The IMF notes that the U.S. remains a key contributor to near-term global growth amid ongoing technology investment, while Europe and other advanced economies are expected to experience more measured recoveries. The IMF projects China’s economy to grow by 4.5% in 2026 as ongoing government-driven fiscal support, along with relative stabilization in trade conditions, help mitigate the effects of longer-term structural challenges. Despite signs of resilience, the IMF continues to highlight risks associated with geopolitics, trade policy and uncertainty regarding productivity gains from artificial intelligence. In addition to macroeconomic factors, policy developments and security considerations remain important factors affecting global energy markets. Sanctions, political instability affecting certain crude oil‑exporting countries and security risks in key shipping corridors have contributed to ongoing uncertainty in global trade flows and may influence the availability, cost and routing of hydrocarbon supplies to global markets. credit_strengths.text: Enterprise Products Partners generates substantial and growing operating cash flow from its fee-based midstream asset base, which supports consistent debt service even as hydrocarbon prices fluctuate. The partnership's operating cash flow has increased steadily over the past three fiscal years, reflecting resilient demand for natural gas transmission and processing services. This cash generation provides a solid foundation for meeting fixed obligations and funding growth capital expenditures.

Interest coverage remains comfortably above sector norms, with operating income covering gross interest expense by a wide margin. This headroom indicates the partnership can absorb moderate earnings volatility without straining its ability to service debt. The coverage ratio benefits from a large fixed-rate debt portfolio and stable operating margins, which are supported by long-term contracts and diversified midstream infrastructure.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses a substantial maturity concentration in the next twelve months, including senior notes due in early part of the year and a revolving credit agreement maturing shortly thereafter. While the partnership maintains access to revolving facilities, refinancing this near-term wall depends on continued capital market access and could pressure liquidity if credit conditions tighten or if operating cash flow declines unexpectedly.

Risk factors highlight that global liquid hydrocarbon markets have shifted into a modest surplus, with non-OPEC supply growth and OPEC+ production cuts easing, placing downward pressure on prices. This macro backdrop could reduce throughput volumes and margins for the partnership's midstream services, potentially weakening cash flow available for debt service if the surplus persists or deepens.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow after capital expenditures covers only a modest portion of total debt, indicating that debt reduction relies on refinancing and cash flow growth rather than retained cash. The partnership's capital expenditure program remains significant, consuming a large share of operating cash flow and limiting the pace of deleveraging. This dynamic keeps leverage elevated relative to potential internal debt paydown.

Net leverage stands below the sector median, suggesting the partnership carries less debt relative to earnings than many peers in the utilities and natural gas transmission space. However, the indicative financial risk profile remains significant, and a moderate decline in EBITDA or increase in debt could push leverage toward the next threshold, potentially affecting refinancing terms and credit availability.

overall_credit_view.text: Enterprise Products Partners presents a stable credit profile supported by resilient midstream cash flows, adequate interest coverage, and leverage below sector medians. The partnership's fee-based business model and diversified asset base mitigate commodity price volatility. However, near-term debt maturities and a soft hydrocarbon price outlook warrant monitoring. We view the credit as investment grade with a stable outlook, contingent on management's ability to refinance upcoming maturities and maintain disciplined capital allocation.

Shareholder distributions and buybacks absorb a meaningful portion of free cash flow, limiting internal deleveraging capacity. While the partnership has demonstrated consistent access to capital markets, reliance on external financing for maturities introduces refinancing risk. We expect leverage to remain within the current tier, but a sustained decline in operating cash flow or a debt-funded acquisition could pressure the indicative financial risk profile. Continued monitoring of distribution policy and capital expenditure discipline is warranted.

credit_strengths.text: Enterprise Products Partners 從其收費式中游資產基礎產生龐大且持續增長嘅營運現金流，即使碳氫化合物價格波動，仍支持穩定嘅債務償付。該合夥企業嘅營運現金流在過去三個財政年度穩步增加，反映天然氣輸送及加工服務需求具韌性。此現金產生為履行固定義務及資助增長資本支出提供穩固基礎。
利息覆蓋率仍遠高於行業常規，營運收入大幅覆蓋總利息支出。此緩衝顯示該合夥企業可吸納適度盈利波動，而不會令其償債能力受壓。覆蓋率受惠於龐大嘅固定利率債務組合及穩定嘅營運利潤率，而後者由長期合約及多元化中游基礎設施支持。

key_risks.text: 債務票據披露未來十二個月有大量到期集中，包括於年初到期嘅優先票據及緊隨其後到期嘅循環信貸協議。雖然該合夥企業維持循環融資渠道，但為此近期到期牆再融資取決於持續嘅資本市場准入，若信貸條件收緊或營運現金流意外下跌，可能對流動性構成壓力。
風險因素強調全球液態碳氫化合物市場已轉為溫和過剩，非OPEC供應增長及OPEC+減產放鬆，對價格構成下行壓力。此宏觀背景可能降低該合夥企業中游服務嘅吞吐量及利潤率，若過剩持續或加深，可能削弱可用於償債嘅現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 資本支出後嘅自由現金流僅覆蓋總債務嘅一小部分，顯示債務削減依賴再融資及現金流增長，而非留存現金。該合夥企業嘅資本支出計劃仍然龐大，消耗營運現金流嘅一大部分，並限制去槓桿速度。此動態令槓桿相對於潛在內部債務償還維持偏高。
淨槓桿低於行業中位數，顯示該合夥企業相對於盈利嘅債務少於公用事業及天然氣輸送領域嘅許多同業。然而，指示性財務風險狀況仍然顯著，EBITDA適度下降或債務增加可能將槓桿推向下一門檻，可能影響再融資條款及信貸可得性。

overall_credit_view.text: Enterprise Products Partners 呈現穩定嘅信貸狀況，受具韌性嘅中游現金流、足夠嘅利息覆蓋率及低於行業中位數嘅槓桿支持。該合夥企業嘅收費式業務模式及多元化資產基礎緩解商品價格波動。然而，近期債務到期及疲軟嘅碳氫化合物價格前景值得監察。我們認為該信貸為投資級，展望穩定，取決於管理層為即將到期債務再融資及維持紀律性資本配置嘅能力。
股東分派及回購吸收自由現金流嘅重要部分，限制內部去槓桿能力。雖然該合夥企業已展示持續嘅資本市場准入，但依賴外部融資應付到期引入再融資風險。我們預期槓桿將維持於當前級別內，但營運現金流持續下降或債務資助收購可能對指示性財務風險狀況構成壓力。持續監察分派政策及資本支出紀律屬恰當。
